title: BusinessWorld Forecast 2027 to tackle economic resilience

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — As the Philippines looks toward 2027, the economic prospects remain shaped by a range of global and domestic pressures, from geopolitical tensions and energy price volatility to climate risks and governance concerns.
While growth is expected to recover, businesses and households remain cautious as inflationary pressures and investment constraints shape the country’s economic outlook.
These challenges and opportunities will take center stage at BusinessWorld Forecast 2027, to be held on Nov. 25 at the Grand Ballroom of the Grand Hyatt Manila in Boni-facio Global City, Taguig.

With the theme “Resilience in Disruption,” the forum will bring together policymakers, economists, business executives and industry leaders to discuss how the Philippines can sustain economic growth, navigate emerging risks, and identify opportunities amid an increasingly uncertain global environment.

Hosted by Philippine Stock Exchange head of market education Jester de los Santos, the whole-day event will serve as a platform for thought leaders to share insights on the country’s economic prospects, investment landscape, and strategies for building long-term resilience.

Three keynote speakers will set the tone for the discussions throughout the day. Department of Economy, Planning, and Development Secretary Arsenio Balisacan will deliver a keynote address “The Philippine Economic Outlook: A Path Through Cautious Recovery,” focusing on the country’s growth prospects and the factors that could influence the country’s recovery in 2027.

SM Investments Corp. president and chief executive officer Frederic DyBuncio will share his insights on the country’s growth opportunities amid current economic challeng-es in “Investing for Resilient Philippine Growth”; while iPeople Inc. president and chief operating officer Alfredo Antonio Ayala will talk about addressing skill gaps and pre-paring Filipino workers for an increasingly digital and artificial intelligence-driven workplace in “Human Capital 2.0: Redefining Education and Talent in the Age of AI.”
Panel discussions will delve deeper into issues in trade and logistics, climate resilience, human capital development, political uncertainty and AI.

The first panel discussion, “The Next Evolution of Trade in the Philippines,” will examine how the country can strengthen its logistics network and supply chain connectivity as retail and e-commerce continue to expand. Panelists will include Department of Finance Assistant Secretary Neil Adrian Cabiles, Philippine Exporters Confederation Inc. president and CEO Dr. Sergio Ortiz-Luis Jr., and Reyes Tacandong & Co. Senior Adviser Jonathan Ravelas, CTA.

“Climate Shock: Can the Philippine Economy Stay Resilient?” will be the focus of the second panel discussion. Experts will examine how climate-related disruptions, including typhoons, flooding, extreme heat, and drought, affect business operations, agricultural production, supply chains, and investment decisions.

Among the confirmed panelists are Department of Agriculture Assistant Secretary for operations and adapting Philippine agriculture to climate change National Project Di-rector U-Nichols Manalo, World Bank Senior Country Economist Jaffar Al-Rikabi, ARISE Philippines chairperson and ARISE Global board member Vice-Admiral Alexander Patino Pama AFP (Ret.), and United Nations Laureate and Asian Science Diplomats chairman and president Sci. Dpl. Glenn Banaguas.

The third panel discussion, titled “Between Politics and Prosperity: Navigating an Uncertain Economy,” will examine how political developments and governance concerns could influence investor confidence, economic policies, and business decisions in the year ahead.
Panelists include Stratbase Group founder and chief executive officer Victor Andres Manhit, and political analysts and columnists Rolando Llamas and Andrew James Masigan.

For the final panel, thought leaders will examine how companies can move beyond AI experimentation and translate technological investments into measurable business value, while addressing concerns involving data quality, cybersecurity, implementation costs, and governance, in a discussion titled “AI in Business: Risks versus Rewards.”

Joining the panel are Globe Telecom president and CEO Carl Raymond Cruz; United Nations Development Programme in the Philippines Country Economist Mohamed Sha-hudh; PLDT senior vice president, head of Enterprise Business Group, and Group AI Business lead Patricio Pineda III; and Boston Consulting Group partner Lance Katigbak.

Through these discussions, BusinessWorld Forecast 2027 aims to gather a wide range of perspectives on how the Philippines can move forward through global uncertainty, economic pressures, and structural disruption.
To register for BusinessWorld Forecast 2027, visit https://businessworldforecast.helixpay.ph/.
